title: The Figure That Was Too Good
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, the Detective Boys/Ai Haibara, Dr. Agasa, Takagi, Megure) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. case_type: murder. The old lower-fidelity case file's culprit (s2, Shunichi Morishita) matches the transcript -- unlike some other rebuilt episodes, the old file's core accusation was correct. What the old file missed/simplified: (1) it collapsed the frame-up of Reika Kameyama into a single generic 'was_at' listing without capturing that Morishita deliberately planted her brooch (smeared with victim's blood) and sent a fake e-mail from the victim's phone to strip her alibi -- this is the actual mechanism the episode is built around, not a side detail; (2) it omitted the comparative forensic clue that no blood was found on Kameyama's clothes despite the brooch being soaked -- the clue that first cracks the frame-up open; (3) it omitted Kenji Hiroto (the reporter, initial red-herring suspect who fled the scene) as a person node entirely; (4) it described the murder weapon only as 'hidden in a bouquet' without capturing that it was pre-painted to blend in as foliage inside that bouquet -- the titular 'figure that was too good' twist (Morishita's paint-matching skill, used both to secretly ghost-model Kitajima's award diorama and to disguise the knife). No stated culprit discrepancy to correct here; enrichment only.

clues.desc: Green paint stains on Morishita's shirt don't match his own brightly colored robots, but match his paint case and Kitajima's diorama exactly.
Kitajima's blood soaked the brooch alone, yet Kameyama's clothes had no bloodstains at all -- a real stabbing splashes the wearer, not just a pinned accessory.
Kitajima had little modeling skill early on, then suddenly became a nature-modeling genius years later, and never let anyone watch him work.
